action: App developers and privacy teams: request photo library access with a separate, specific consent, keep such features off by default and explain how to disable them. Facebook users on Android can review the app's photo permission in phone settings.
exec: A very large fine under ePrivacy device-access rules, outside the GDPR one-stop shop; Meta has 60 days to make the feature opt-in.
plain: Italy's privacy regulator fined Meta 805 million euros because the Facebook app on Android phones could read people's photo galleries by default without specific consent, affecting about 20 million people.

key_findings: Meta Platforms Ireland was fined EUR 805 million, roughly 0.47 per cent of the group's global turnover.
The Facebook Android app accessed photos, videos and metadata through a camera-roll suggestions feature enabled by default since 2023, behind one vague app-wide permission.
About 20 million Android users in Italy are affected; the inquiry began in July 2025 after a complaint from a Bolzano consumer centre.
The breach is of Article 122 of the Italian Privacy Code; the Garante rejected Meta's argument that the Irish authority was competent, as ePrivacy has no one-stop shop.
report.publisher: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali
recommendations: Within 60 days Meta must obtain separate, specific consent for the feature and explain its purpose, its camera-roll access and how to disable it.
The feature must be off by default, including for users who already granted the permission.
Meta must report initiatives begun within 30 days and measures adopted within 90 days.

summary: Italy's Garante fined Meta Platforms Ireland EUR 805 million because the Facebook app on Android reached users' photos, videos and metadata through a camera-roll suggestions feature that was on by default from 2023, without specific consent or clear information. About 20 million Android users in Italy are affected. The breach is of Article 122 of the Italian Privacy Code, the ePrivacy rule on device access. Press reports say Meta will appeal.
title: Italy fines Meta 805 million euros over Facebook's access to Android photo galleries
